sentences.text: Yes, the autoimmune regulator (Aire) has been found to be inducibly expressed in human and mouse tumor keratinocytes.
Aire expression in these skin tumor cells depends on keratin 17 (K17), which is upregulated in many epithelial tumors.
In mice, Aire is required for the timely onset of Gli2-induced skin tumorigenesis.
Aire is best known for driving the expression of tissue-specific self-antigens in medullary thymic epithelial cells to enforce central tolerance.
Aire protein has also been detected outside the thymus, in peripheral lymphoid organs.
The evidence indicates the opposite: CX3CR1 promotes, rather than impairs, the survival of T helper cells in the inflamed lung.
In people with asthma, a fraction of CD4+ T cells express CX3CR1, the receptor for the chemokine CX3CL1.
CX3CR1-deficient mice, or wild-type mice treated with CX3CR1-blocking reagents, show reduced allergic lung disease.
Transferring wild-type CD4+ T cells into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored the cardinal features of asthma.
Other factors, such as the transcription factor Blimp-1, also shape Th2 cell differentiation and function.
No, the evidence suggests ultrasound guidance reduces rather than raises the number of traumatic needle insertion procedures.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials compared ultrasound imaging with standard palpation for lumbar punctures and epidural catheterisations.
Ultrasound imaging was associated with a lower risk of failed procedures than palpation methods.
Ultrasound also reduced the number of insertion attempts and needle redirections.
Diagnostic lumbar punctures are associated with adverse events, which motivates techniques that lower procedural risk.
IFIT1 is an interferon-induced protein that restricts viruses whose RNA lacks proper 2'-O methylation of the 5' cap, by binding and sequestering these mis-capped RNAs from translation.
Viruses that replicate in the cytoplasm cannot access the host nuclear capping machinery and so encode their own methyltransferases to cap their RNA.
2'-O methylation of the viral RNA cap mimics cellular mRNA and helps viruses evade host innate immune restriction.
A virus defective in 2'-O methylation is recognized and eliminated by the host immune response, which has been exploited to design attenuated flavivirus vaccines.
Coronavirus mutants lacking 2'-O-methyltransferase activity also induce higher type I interferon expression via the RNA sensor Mda5.
Yes, primary pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1beta trigger cascades of secondary inflammatory mediators in target cells.
In synovial fibroblasts, IL-1beta stimulation induces an inflammatory response that can be attenuated by curcumin.
IL-1beta itself is processed by inflammasomes, multiprotein complexes linking pathogen recognition and cellular stress to cytokine maturation.
These cytokine cascades include both pro-inflammatory mediators such as prostaglandins and chemokines and anti-inflammatory mediators such as IL-10 that help resolve inflammation.
Yes, transplanted human glial progenitor cells can mature and differentiate within a host animal's brain.
When human glial progenitor cells were engrafted into neonatal immunodeficient mice, the recipient brains later contained large numbers of human astrocytes.
The engrafted human glia were gap-junction-coupled to host astroglia while retaining the size and complexity of human astrocytes.
Mice engrafted with human glia showed enhanced synaptic plasticity and learning.
Neural precursors derived from human embryonic stem cells can also differentiate into neurons and glia after transplantation into the rodent brain.
Research indicates that Tetraspanin 3 is required for the development and propagation of acute myelogenous leukemia (AML).
Tetraspanin 3 is a target of the RNA-binding protein Musashi 2, which plays a key role in AML.
Deleting Tspan3 in mice impaired leukemia stem cell self-renewal and disease propagation.
Tspan3 deletion also markedly improved survival in mouse models of AML.
AML can also arise from other genetic events, such as the t(8;21) translocation that produces the AML1-ETO fusion transcript.
In adult humans, the majority of T cells residing in tissues such as mucosal sites and lymphoid organs have a memory phenotype.
By contrast, in early life most tissue T cells are naive, with memory T cells accumulating with age and antigen exposure.
Many of these memory cells are tissue-resident memory T cells that provide enhanced regional immunity.
CD4 tissue-resident memory T cells in the genital mucosa, for example, are maintained by a local macrophage chemokine network.
Yes, CX3CR1 is required for allergic airway inflammation.
Mice lacking CX3CR1, or treated with CX3CR1-blocking reagents, show reduced lung disease after allergen sensitization and challenge.
CX3CR1 acts by promoting the survival and maintenance of T helper cells in the inflamed lung.
Allergic asthma is a Th2-dominated disease, and CD11b+ dendritic cells are key initiators of Th2 immunity to house dust mite allergen.
The cytokine IL-33 can also promote asthma pathogenesis by expanding Th2 cells.
Evidence from intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) suggests that prior use of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) is associated with lower in-hospital mortality than prior warfarin use.
This finding comes from a retrospective cohort of 141,311 ICH patients admitted to 1,662 Get With The Guidelines-Stroke hospitals between 2013 and 2016.
Compared with no oral anticoagulant use, both warfarin and NOAC use were associated with higher in-hospital mortality after ICH.
Low plasma levels of direct oral anticoagulants have been linked to thrombotic complications in high-risk atrial fibrillation patients.
In Xenopus embryos, the dorsal Spemann organizer secretes ADMP together with the BMP antagonist Chordin, forming a dorsal activator-inhibitor pair.
ADMP and BMP2/4/7 are regulated at opposite embryonic poles to generate a self-regulating morphogenetic field.
ADMP transcription in the Spemann organizer is activated when BMP levels are low.
Quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 eliminates self-regulation and causes ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.
Chordin acts as an antagonist of ventralizing BMPs, and its facilitated degradation helps dorsal-ventral patterning scale with embryo size.
Formation of the central supramolecular activation cluster (cSMAC) influences how strongly a T cell responds to a given peptide-MHC ligand.
A peptide with many hallmarks of a weak agonist was found to stimulate T cells to proliferate more than the wild-type agonist ligand.
Modeling suggested that the inability to form a cSMAC could explain this enhanced response, meaning cSMAC formation can attenuate rather than enhance signalling for some ligands.
TCR-proximal signals are initiated and sustained in peripheral microclusters, whereas signalling is terminated in the cSMAC.
The cSMAC is enriched in lysobisphosphatidic acid, a lipid involved in sorting ubiquitinated membrane proteins for degradation.
ML-SA1 is a synthetic small-molecule agonist that activates the lysosomal TRPML channels, including TRPML1 and TRPML2.
Cryo-EM structures indicate that ML-SA1 binds in a hydrophobic pocket formed by the S5, S6 and pore helix regions of TRPML channels.

Because the ML-SA1 binding pocket residues are largely conserved between TRPML1 and TRPML2, the two channels would be expected to bind ML-SA1 in a broadly similar way, although direct structural comparison of TRPML2 is limited.
No, aneuploidy appears to be relatively common in domesticated Saccharomyces cerevisiae, especially industrial strains.
Genome sequencing of 157 industrial S. cerevisiae yeasts showed they form five sublineages separate from wild strains.
Industrial beer yeasts frequently show signs of domestication such as polyploidy and aneuploidy, in contrast to most wild isolates.
Faithful chromosome segregation in S. cerevisiae depends on the centromeric histone H3 variant Cse4, whose phosphorylation regulates segregation.

Loss of the atypical protein kinase C zeta (PKCzeta) has been reported to enhance tumour growth by allowing cancer cells to reprogram their nutrient metabolism, including glutamine use, under nutrient stress.
Many cancer cells rely heavily on glutamine to fuel anabolic processes.
Pancreatic cancer cells use a non-canonical, Kras-regulated pathway of glutamine metabolism that is required for tumour growth.
Glutamine metabolism through glutaminolysis also activates Rag-mTORC1 signalling, which promotes cell growth.
The coactivator SRC-2 drives glutamine-dependent de novo lipogenesis that supports prostate cancer survival and metastasis.
Two-component systems consist of histidine kinases that phosphorylate their cognate response regulators to let bacteria respond to signals.
Phosphotransfer between histidine kinases and response regulators is generally highly specific.
This specificity is tightly controlled to prevent unwanted crosstalk among the many two-component pathways a bacterium may possess.
Fidelity is thought to arise mainly from molecular recognition, with kinetic preference meaning cognate pairs undergo phosphotransfer much faster than non-cognate pairs.
Specificity residues at the kinase-regulator interface determine binding affinity between these partners.
No, ALDH1 expression is generally associated with worse, not better, breast cancer outcomes.
Mammary epithelial cells with high aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) activity have stem or progenitor properties.
ALDH1 marks both normal and malignant human mammary stem cells.
ALDH1 expression in breast tumours has been reported as a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
Other markers, such as high infiltration of tumor-associated macrophages, also predict unfavorable outcomes in node-negative breast cancer.
Yes, CK-666 is a small-molecule inhibitor that binds the Arp2/3 complex and blocks its actin nucleation activity.
These inhibitors allow the Arp2/3 complex to be inhibited reversibly in living cells.
Pharmacological inhibition of the Arp2/3 complex radically alters lamellipodial actin architecture.
Arp2/3 inhibition also changes suspended cell shape and the cell spreading process.
The WAVE2 complex relays signals from Rac to the Arp2/3 complex to drive lamellipodia protrusion.
Thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) methylates mercaptopurine to methylmercaptopurine, which is a catabolic inactivation step rather than an anabolic one.
Genetic variation in TPMT is associated with life-threatening leukopenia during thiopurine therapy.
A common missense variant in NUDT15 also confers susceptibility to thiopurine-induced leukopenia, particularly in Asian populations.
The active metabolites of mercaptopurine are thioguanine nucleotides, whose red blood cell levels have correlated with event-free survival in childhood leukemia.
Yes, ivermectin is used in mass drug administration programs against lymphatic filariasis, typically combined with albendazole in Africa.
Lymphatic filariasis is a neglected tropical disease that has seen substantial reductions in prevalence and incidence over recent decades.
Integrated 'rapid-impact' packages that combine drugs such as ivermectin, albendazole and praziquantel can control several neglected tropical diseases at once.
Ivermectin is also the mainstay drug for controlling onchocerciasis.
Yes, the b-wave of the flash-evoked electroretinogram (ERG) is widely understood to reflect the activity of ON-bipolar cells.
Mice carrying the X-linked 'no b-wave' (nob) mutation lack the ERG b-wave because visual transmission between photoreceptors and second-order neurons is compromised.
The nob mouse serves as a naturally occurring model of X-linked congenital stationary night blindness.
In the ERG, the preceding a-wave reflects photoreceptor activity, while the b-wave arises downstream in the inner retina.
The evidence points the other way: increasing tumour vascularity and reducing stromal fibrosis tends to improve chemotherapy delivery and efficacy.
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumours are poorly perfused and poorly vascularized, which contributes to their insensitivity to drugs such as gemcitabine.
In a mouse model of pancreatic cancer, inhibiting Hedgehog signaling depleted tumour stroma, increased vessel density and enhanced gemcitabine delivery.
Extracellular matrix stiffness can also reduce responses to targeted therapy, such as the HER2 inhibitor lapatinib, via YAP and TAZ.
Yes, venules generally have larger lumen diameters than the arterioles that feed the same capillary bed.
Venules have thinner walls with less smooth muscle, so their lumens are wider relative to wall thickness than those of arterioles.
Arterioles, in contrast, have thick muscular walls that regulate vascular tone and resistance, for example via endothelium-mediated relaxation.
Dilation of cerebral microvessels in response to nitric oxide is mediated largely by soluble guanylate cyclase.
No, ribosomopathies are notable for producing strikingly cell- and tissue-specific pathology despite ribosomes being needed in every cell.
Defects in ribosome biogenesis underlie a growing number of symptomatically distinct inherited disorders called ribosomopathies.
Mutations in RPS19 and other ribosomal protein genes cause Diamond-Blackfan anemia, which mainly affects red blood cell production.
Other ribosomopathies include Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, dyskeratosis congenita and cartilage hair hypoplasia, each with distinct clinical features.
Loss of the ribosome biogenesis factor Nol11 in Xenopus specifically disrupts craniofacial development.
Umbilical cord blood (UCB) T cells are predominantly naive, but after transplantation they undergo expansion and acquire a memory-like phenotype in recipients.
UCB is widely used as an alternative hematopoietic stem cell source for patients lacking matched adult donors.
UCB transplantation has traditionally been associated with delayed engraftment and poor immune reconstitution.
The cumulative incidence of serious infections after pediatric UCB transplantation was comparable to that after bone marrow transplantation.
Bariatric surgery is associated with sustained weight loss and improved physical health in severely obese individuals.
Mental health conditions such as depression and binge eating disorder are common among patients seeking bariatric surgery.
Bariatric surgery has been associated with postoperative decreases in the prevalence of depression and the severity of depressive symptoms.
Long-term follow-up studies report improvements in psychological and psychosocial functioning several years after restrictive bariatric surgery.
Guidelines recommend that behavioral health clinicians be involved in the evaluation and care of bariatric patients both before and after surgery.
Yes, evidence suggests open-access articles are more likely to be cited than non-open-access articles.
A study by Gunther Eysenbach published in PLoS Biology found that open-access articles are more immediately recognized and cited than non-OA articles.
Proponents argue that open-access publication speeds up scientific dialogue between researchers.
The size of this citation advantage varies across fields and studies, and some analyses attribute part of it to self-selection of higher-quality papers for open access.
Yes, knockin mice in which gp130-dependent SHP2 signalling is disrupted develop lymphadenopathy.
These SHP2 signal-deficient mice (gp130F759/F759) were born normal but displayed splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy.
The SHP2 signal-deficient mice also showed an enhanced acute phase reaction.
In contrast, mice deficient in gp130-mediated STAT3 signalling died perinatally, indicating reciprocal roles for STAT3 and SHP2 signals.
Constitutive activation of SHP-2 causes Noonan syndrome and perturbs neural cell-fate decisions.
Yes, PPARs function as heterodimers with retinoid X receptors (RXRs), and these PPAR-RXR complexes are activated by PPAR ligands.
For example, the PPARalpha ligand fenofibrate decreased the metastatic potential of melanoma cells via down-regulation of Akt.
Pharmacological activation of PPARgamma signaling ameliorated disease severity in Cftr-deficient mice.
Retinoid receptor heterodimers such as RAR/RXR recruit transcriptional coactivators in a ligand-dependent manner.
RXR heterodimers with other partners, such as liver X receptors, can likewise be activated by their ligands, for instance to prevent bacterial-induced macrophage apoptosis.
Golli protein, an alternatively spliced product of the myelin basic protein gene, negatively regulates calcium influx in T cells.
Golli-deficient T cells show enhanced calcium entry upon T cell receptor stimulation.
Rather than becoming anergic, Golli-deficient T cells are hyperproliferative.
Calcium entry through CRAC channels activates the transcription factor NFAT to promote immune responses.
Golli gene products are expressed in primary lymphoid organs such as the thymus during development.
No, Ly6C-high monocytes are generally considered the more inflammatory subset, not the less inflammatory one.
Mouse blood monocytes consist of two principal subsets with distinct migratory properties.
The short-lived CX3CR1-low CCR2+ Gr1+ (Ly6C-high) subset is actively recruited to inflamed tissues.
The CX3CR1-high CCR2- Gr1- (Ly6C-low) subset is recruited to non-inflamed tissues in a CX3CR1-dependent manner.
In inflammatory arthritis models, greater numbers of the inflammatory Ly6C+ monocyte subset are recruited to the site of inflammation.
When upstream Hippo kinases are inactive, YAP and its paralogue TAZ are dephosphorylated, stabilized and translocate into the nucleus.
In the nucleus, YAP acts as a transcriptional coactivator that binds TEAD family transcription factors.
TEAD is essential for YAP-dependent gene expression, cell growth and oncogenic transformation.
CTGF has been identified as a direct target gene of the YAP-TEAD complex.
TEAD itself can be regulated by p38 MAPK-induced translocation to the cytoplasm, which suppresses YAP-driven transcription.
Evidence suggests that macrolide antibiotics do not significantly lower the risk of a first acute myocardial infarction.
The question arose because certain bacterial infections, such as Chlamydia pneumoniae, have been hypothesized to increase the risk of acute myocardial infarction.
A large case-control study found that prior use of tetracyclines or quinolones was associated with a reduced risk of first-time myocardial infarction.
In the same study, no such protective association was found for macrolides, sulfonamides, penicillins or cephalosporins.
Large randomized trials of macrolides such as azithromycin for secondary prevention of coronary events have also failed to show a benefit.
Evidence indicates that hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) segregate their chromosomes randomly rather than asymmetrically.
The 'immortal strand' hypothesis proposed that stem cells retain older DNA strands while new strands go to differentiating daughter cells.
Studies in mice found that HSCs neither asymmetrically segregate chromosomes nor retain BrdU labels.
Mouse hematopoietic stem cells can be purified using phenotypic markers and can reconstitute all blood cell types in irradiated recipients.
Evidence generally indicates the opposite: improving structural, logistical and interpersonal elements tends to enhance, not impair, healthcare delivery efficiency in crowded facilities.
Healthcare is a complex industry in which errors often stem from failures within the system rather than individual blame.
Strengthening system design is therefore seen as a key route to safer and more efficient care.
Studies comparing healthcare structures, such as teaching versus nonteaching hospitals, show that organizational context can influence patient outcomes.
Metastases often share the major driver mutations of their primary tumour, but they also frequently acquire additional genomic changes, so similarity is substantial but not complete.
Genomic alterations that activate cyclin/cdk complexes, such as deletion of p16INK4a or p18INK4c, drive tumours like glioblastoma.
Genomic aberrations can also accumulate in cultured pluripotent stem cells, illustrating how genomes diverge under selective pressure.
In BRCA1 mutation carriers, aberrant luminal progenitors have been proposed as the cell of origin for basal-like breast tumours.
The evidence does not support a clear protective effect of macrolides against myocardial infarction.
Interest in antibiotics stems from the hypothesis that certain bacterial infections increase the risk of acute myocardial infarction.
In a large case-control analysis, tetracycline and quinolone users had a lower risk of first-time myocardial infarction, but macrolide users did not.
Other cardioprotective mechanisms are being explored, such as IL-33 signaling through ST2, which reduced apoptosis and improved survival after experimental myocardial infarction.
No, high CRP levels are associated with an increased, not reduced, risk of COPD exacerbations.
A prospective Copenhagen cohort study of 61,650 participants tested whether elevated inflammatory biomarkers in stable COPD predict exacerbations.
Individuals with stable COPD and elevated CRP, fibrinogen and leukocyte count had a higher risk of exacerbations.
A history of prior exacerbations is the strongest predictor of future exacerbations, reflecting a frequent-exacerbator phenotype.
TNF-alpha and IL-1 are classic pro-inflammatory cytokines, but they generally stimulate rather than inhibit IL-6 and IL-10 production.
Elevated circulating levels of IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha appear together during inflammatory responses, including the one induced by physical activity.
TNF-alpha and IL-6 levels have been linked to the development of cachexia in patients with non-small cell lung cancer.
IL-1 and TNF also alter glucose turnover when infused in rats.
Input from mental and physical health professionals can improve the wellbeing of homeless people, though evidence that it alone reduces homelessness is limited.
A mental health outreach service for homeless families was associated with improvements in short-term psychosocial functioning of children and parents.
Homeless children and their mothers have high rates of mental health problems that persist after rehousing.
Homeless people face increased risk of premature death and significant barriers to accessing health care.
Approaches that combine housing with health and social support, such as Housing First, have been the most effective at reducing homelessness.
